### 3. ToolHitContext / Hit System

**How hits flow:**

```

  ↓ reads _aimer.WorldAimPoint, _aimer.HoveredGameObject, _aimer.SwingAnimIndex
  ↓ calls _playerInit.EmitHit(point, target, damage)

- Wrench controllers are single-responsibility.

```csharp
public class Billboard : MonoBehaviour
{
    private Camera _mainCamera;
    private void Start() { _mainCamera = Camera.main; }
    private void LateUpdate()
    {
        if (_mainCamera == null) return;
        Vector3 directionToCamera = _mainCamera.transform.position - transform.position;
        float horizontalDist = new Vector2(directionToCamera.x, directionToCamera.z).magnitude;
        float pitchAngle = Mathf.Atan2(directionToCamera.y, horizontalDist) * Mathf.Rad2Deg;
        transform.rotation = Quaternion.Euler(pitchAngle, transform.eulerAngles.y, 0f);
    }
}
```

**How it works:** Pitches the sprite toward the camera each LateUpdate, preserving the object's Y-rotation. This means the sprite tilts up/down based on camera elevation but maintains its world-facing direction.

- `Start` vs `Awake` — if a `ResourceDeathFall` component needs to disable this in `OnEnable`->`HandleDepleted`, the `_mainCamera` might not be set yet. Should use `Awake`.
- **Not disabled when camera is null** — it silently returns. No logging.

- **Grounded check:** Raycast from collider base.

**What works well:**
- Smart use of force-based movement — physics composes naturally with AddForce zones, drag, friction.
- Per-step reset of terrain modifiers prevents stale state when leaving a zone.
- LowGrip grace timer is a thoughtful solution to trigger gap flicker.
- Clean separation: zone sets properties, controller reads them.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **No shared terrain state** — each zone independently sets controller properties. No composite effect system (e.g., wind + water = different behaviour).
- **OnTriggerStay** is less reliable than `OnTriggerEnter/Exit` + tracking your own state. If the Rigidbody sleeps or teleports, the stay event can miss a frame.
- **No effect priority** — if two zones overlap, last OnTriggerStay wins (race condition).
- **Controller properties are public mutable fields** — any script can stomp them. Should be `{ get; set; }` on an interface or use a struct.
- **No terrain state SO** — zone-to-controller coupling is tight. Could use a `TerrainState` SO that aggregates all zone effects.
- **MoveInput reads Input.GetAxisRaw** directly — no input abstraction layer.
- **Jump is always the same height** — no variable jump.

---

### 8. RopeLassoController

**File:** `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/RopeLassoController.cs`
**Also read:** `RopeLassoConfig.cs`, `RopeAnchor.cs`, `RopePullable.cs`

**Structure:** MonoBehaviour with `[RequireComponent(typeof(PlayerMouseAimer))]`.

**Public API:**
- `IsCharging`, `ChargeNormalized`, `IsPulling`, `HandPoint`

**How it works:**
- Hold Q to charge (no gameplay effect — fires on release regardless).
- On release: reads `_aimer.HoveredAnchor` and `_aimer.HoveredPullable` + `HoveredGrapplePoint`.
- Range-gated against `_config.minRange` / `_config.maxRange`.
- If RopePullable → `BeginPull(selfPull: false)`: reels object to player.
- If RopeAnchor → `BeginPull(selfPull: true)`: reels player to anchor point.
- Winch is force-based (AddForce) with speed cap. Self-pull suppresses steering (can't fight the reel).
- LineRenderer draws the rope from HandPoint to the far end while pulling.
- **Mud check:** reads `_controller.CanJump` (which TerrainEffectZone sets false on mud).

**What works well:**
- Clean dual-mode (pull object / pull self).
- Force-based winch composes with physics.
- LineRenderer rope is simple and effective.
- Collision detection via aimer raycast (no separate trigger volume).

**What needs refactoring:**
- **Terrain interaction is fragile** — the mud check reads `CanJump` as a proxy, which is a side effect of the mud zone setting that property. Should have an explicit `IsInMud` property on the controller.
- **No cooldown on failed grapple** — if you miss/out-of-range, the charge still consumed and nothing happens (poor UX feedback).
- **No break force** — the pull runs until distance or timeout. No collision/wall break detection.
- **LineRenderer re-enabled every frame** — minor, but `LateUpdate` writes to `_ropeLine.enabled` every frame whether pulling or not.
- **Hard singleton dependency** on `PlayerInventory.Instance` for the wrench check.

---

### 9. Billboard.cs

**File:** `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Common/Billboard.cs`

**Full source (21 lines):**
```csharp
public class Billboard : MonoBehaviour
{
    private Camera _mainCamera;
    private void Start() { _mainCamera = Camera.main; }
    private void LateUpdate()
    {
        if (_mainCamera == null) return;
        Vector3 directionToCamera = _mainCamera.transform.position - transform.position;
        float horizontalDist = new Vector2(directionToCamera.x, directionToCamera.z).magnitude;
        float pitchAngle = Mathf.Atan2(directionToCamera.y, horizontalDist) * Mathf.Rad2Deg;
        transform.rotation = Quaternion.Euler(pitchAngle, transform.eulerAngles.y, 0f);
    }
}
```

**How it works:** Pitches the sprite toward the camera each LateUpdate, preserving the object's Y-rotation. This means the sprite tilts up/down based on camera elevation but maintains its world-facing direction.

**What works well:** Simple, single-responsibility, efficient (no allocations).

**What needs refactoring:**
- Uses `Camera.main` (FindObjectOfType performance hit — should cache via event or injection).
- `Start` vs `Awake` — if a `ResourceDeathFall` component needs to disable this in `OnEnable`->`HandleDepleted`, the `_mainCamera` might not be set yet. Should use `Awake`.
- **Not disabled when camera is null** — it silently returns. No logging.
- No option for different billboard modes (e.g., full billboard vs Y-only vs pitch-only).
- The comment mentions "pitchAngle" but the Y rotation is preserved — this is a semi-billboard (tilted sprite). Clearer naming/modes would help.

---

### 10. UIManager + PlayerHudPanel + WorldInteractTagPresenter

**Files read:**
- `Assets/Flynn/UI/Core/UIManager.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/UI/Screens/PlayerHud/PlayerHudPanel.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/UI/Screens/InteractTag/InteractTagPanel.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/UI/Core/MousePointer.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/WorldInteractTagPresenter.cs`

**UIManager** (`UI/Core/UIManager.cs`):
- Singleton (`Instance`), -100 execution order.
- **Inbound signals:** `SignalShow(UIPanelId)`, `SignalHide(UIPanelId)`, `SignalToggle(UIPanelId)`.
- **Outbound events:** `OnPanelShown(UIPanelId)`, `OnPanelHidden(UIPanelId)`.
- Registry of `IUIPanel` panels by `UIPanelId`. Serialized list + runtime registration.
- No knowledge of concrete panels — works entirely by id.

**PlayerHudPanel** (`UI/Screens/PlayerHud/PlayerHudPanel.cs`):
- Extends `UIToolkitPanel`. Always-visible HUD: hotbar, echo shard counter, battery gauge.
- **Sources:** `PlayerInventory` (for hotbar), `IntVariable` for echo shards, `IntVariable` for battery.
- **Event-driven:** subscribes to `inventory.OnSlotChanged`, `inventory.OnActiveSlotChanged`, `echoShards.OnChanged`, `battery.OnChanged`.
- **Binding:** Query VisualElement tree by ID (`Slot_0`, `Icon_0`, `Count_0`, `EchoCount`, `BatteryFill`, `BatteryLabel`).

**InteractTagPanel** (`UI/Screens/InteractTag/InteractTagPanel.cs`):
- Follows mouse cursor. `Show(text)` displays the tag, `HideTag()` hides it.
- Driven by `WorldInteractTagPresenter` each LateUpdate.

**WorldInteractTagPresenter** (`Scripts/Player/WorldInteractTagPresenter.cs`):
- Reads `_aimer.HoveredInteractable` each LateUpdate.
- If valid and `TryGetPrompt(out prompt)` → calls `_tagPanel.Show(prompt.Display)`.
- Otherwise → `_tagPanel.HideTag()`.
- NOTE: Has a fake-null check: `if (hovered is UnityEngine.Object obj && obj == null)` — this catches destroyed Unity objects.

**MousePointer** (`UI/Core/MousePointer.cs`):
- Singleton (`Instance`), -90 execution order.
- One raycast per frame against combined `_worldMask`. Caches: `ScreenPosition`, `WorldRay`, `HasHit`, `Hit`, `WorldPoint`, `HoverCollider`, `HoverObject`.
- Event: `OnHoverChanged(GameObject)`.
- All gameplay systems read from this cache instead of casting their own rays.

**What works well:**
- **UIManager's signal/event pattern** is excellent — gameplay systems fire signals, UI reacts. No direct coupling.
- **Event-driven HUD** — no Update polling, just event handlers. Battery and echo shards use IntVariable events.
- **MousePointer single raycast** — eliminates 5+ redundant raycasts per frame.
- **InteractTagPresenter correctly handles destroyed Unity objects** (fake-null check via `is UnityEngine.Object`).

**What needs refactoring:**
- **UIManager is tightly coupled to UIPanelId enum** — adding new panels requires modifying the enum. Should be string-keyed or use a more extensible pattern.
- **No IUI panel interface defined in the read files** — `IUIPanel` and `UIPanelId` are in other files not in Flynn/Scripts (likely in the UI folder's non-Script files).
- **PlayerHudPanel hardcodes 4 slots** via `InventoryData.SlotCount`. When adding more slots, this class needs changes.
- **WorldInteractTagPresenter has find-fallback** (`FindObjectOfType<PlayerMouseAimer>`) — should fail loudly if not wired in inspector.
- **No screen transition system** — UIManager shows/hides panels instantly. No animation hooks.
- **No input abstraction** — MousePointer reads `Input.mousePosition` directly.

---

### 11. HittableSurface

**File:** `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/HittableSurface.cs`

Already covered in section 4. Summary:
- Enum `SurfaceMaterial { Wood, Metal, Rock }`.
- `AttackAnimIndex` maps material to tool: Wood→2(Axe), Metal→3(Hammer), Rock→1(Pick).
- **Does not take damage** — purely cosmetic tool-swap for the wrench swing animation.
- Used by PlayerMouseAimer when the cursor is over a non-resource surface within melee range.

**What works well:** Simple, single responsibility.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **No game mechanic** — swinging at a HittableSurface does nothing. The animation plays, the hit event fires, but ResourceManager ignores non-resource targets. Need destructible world objects or at least feedback.
- **Material enum doesn't map to ItemType** — should reuse ItemType or share a tool-effectiveness table.

---

### 12. FeedbackManager / AudioManager

**Search result: NO FeedbackManager or AudioManager exists anywhere in the project.**

I searched:
- `glob` for `**/*Feedback*.*` → No results
- `glob` for `**/*Audio*.*` → No results
- `search_file_content` for `FeedbackManager|AudioManager` across the entire Flynn directory → only matched the RobotBattery string reference to "PlayerHudPanel"

**This is a critical gap.** There is:
- No centralized VFX feedback system (hit sparks, break effects, UI flash).
- No audio manager (no SFX, no music, no ambience).
- Hit feedback is handled per-component: ResourceShake (positional nudge), WrenchSwingArc (line+ring VFX on the player), ResourceDeathFall (topple/fade).
- No feedback event bus — each system fires its own effects independently.

---

### Cross-Cutting Observations

**Common patterns across the codebase:**
1. **Singleton managers** — ResourceManager, PlayerInventory, RobotBattery, UIManager, MousePointer all use `Instance` pattern with duplicate protection. All run at negative execution order.
2. **SO Event Channels** — ResourceHitChannel, DialogueTriggerChannel, RecalledKnowledgeChannel. Simple `Action<>` events in ScriptableObjects.
3. **Events for HUD binding** — PlayerInventory slot changes, IntVariable changes drive UI reactively.
4. **Value types for data** — PlayerHitInfo (readonly struct), InventorySlot (struct), InteractionPrompt (readonly struct), DialogueTriggerPayload (struct).
5. **PlayerMouseAimer as central resolver** — all hover detection goes through one component, which reads MousePointer's single raycast.

**What needs to be preserved (strengths):**
- Event-driven architecture (ResourceManager → ResourceNode, Inventory → HUD)
- SO-driven configuration (ItemDefinition, ResourceNodeConfig, WrenchConfig, RopeLassoConfig)
- Value types for immutable data (minimize GC alloc)
- Single raycast via MousePointer
- IPlayerVisual interface decouples combat from renderer
- IInteractionPromptProvider interface for generic interactables
- Signals pattern for inbound events

**Critical gaps for MVP:**
1. **No damage multiplier / tool effectiveness** — wrench deals 1 damage regardless of target
2. **No ranged damage** — thrown wrench does no damage
3. **No destructible non-resource objects** — HittableSurface is cosmetic only
4. **No audio** — zero sound anywhere
5. **No feedback system** — no centralized VFX, no screen shake, no UI flash
6. **No inventory persistence** — all state resets on domain reload
7. **No battery cost for actions** — battery drains passively at 1/s, actions cost nothing
8. **No composite terrain effects** — overlapping zones have race conditions
9. **No input abstraction** — Input.GetAxisRaw, Input.GetMouseButton spread everywhere
10. **No service locator / DI** — hard singleton dependencies throughout
11. **No object pooling** — Instantiate/Destroy for every wrench throw and resource drop

**Recommended refactoring priorities:**
1. Introduce a `GameEventBus` that consolidates all SO channels into one typed event system
2. Create a unified `HitContext` that bundles point, normal, tool, damage, source
3. Build `FeedbackManager` and `AudioManager` — key event listeners that play VFX/SFX based on event type
4. Add `ToolEffectivenessTable` SO — maps tool×resource to damage multiplier
5. Extract `IInventory` interface from PlayerInventory
6. Build `ITerrainState` interface or shared SO for composable terrain effects
7. Create `IInputService` interface to abstract Input access
8. Extract `IMousePointer` interface from MousePointer singleton

## Complete Codebase Analysis: `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/` — MVP Architecture Overhaul

I have read every C# file in the Flynn/Scripts directory (108 files), plus all relevant UI/Core files. Here is a thorough per-section report.

---

### 1. GameEventBus / Channel System

**Files read:**
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Common/ResourceHitChannel.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/NPC/Runtime/Triggers/DialogueTriggerChannel.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/NPC/Runtime/Triggers/DialogueTriggerPayload.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/NPC/Runtime/Triggers/DialogueTriggerListener.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/NPC/Runtime/Memory/RecalledKnowledgeChannel.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/NPC/Runtime/Debug/LlmDebugBus.cs`

**Three ScriptableObject-based channels exist:**

| Channel | File | Event Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ResourceHitChannel** | `Common/ResourceHitChannel.cs` | `Action<ResourceNode, float>` | Raised per hit so the HUD can show a world-anchored HP bar |
| **DialogueTriggerChannel** | `NPC/Runtime/Triggers/DialogueTriggerChannel.cs` | `Action<DialogueTriggerPayload>` | NP dialogue triggers — signal ids, source NpcId, handler, payload JSON |
| **RecalledKnowledgeChannel** | `NPC/Runtime/Memory/RecalledKnowledgeChannel.cs` | `Action` (event only) | Carries semantic-recall results per dialogue turn for the NPC Info HUD |

**Additionally there is a static debug bus:**
- **LlmDebugBus** (`NPC/Runtime/Debug/LlmDebugBus.cs`) — static, not SO. Debug-only, holds per-stage/turn records for an LLM debug window.

**Structure pattern:** All SO channels follow: `public event Action<...> OnXxx` + `public void Raise(...)`. This is a **simple C# event wrapper in a ScriptableObject** — no typed event bus, no decoupled messaging system. `DialogueTriggerListener` subscribes/unsubscribes in `OnEnable/OnDisable` and filters by `triggerKey` + optional `npcId`.

**What works well:** Clean decoupling via SO asset refs (no FindObjectOfType for channels). Listeners are self-contained.

**What needs refactoring:**
- No unified event bus. Three separate channel SOs with the same pattern — should be consolidated into a single `GameEventBus` that supports typed events or a common `IEventChannel` interface.
- No centralised subscription management. Each listener manually subscribes/unsubscribes.
- The `LlmDebugBus` is static (non-SO) — violates the SO-variable pattern used everywhere else.

---

### 2. PlayerMouseAimer — Full Source

**File:** `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/PlayerMouseAimer.cs`

**Structure:** `MonoBehaviour` with `[RequireComponent(typeof(SolarpunkCharacterController))]`

**Public Properties (read-only):**
- `WorldAimPoint` (Vector3) — world-space cursor target
- `HoveredResource` (ResourceNode) — resource under cursor, range-gated by `_interactionRange`
- `HoveredPickup` (WorldItemPickup) — deprecated legacy pickup
- `HoveredKeyPickup` (WorldItem) — non-auto-collect world items (e.g. wrench), range-gated
- `HoveredAnchor` (RopeAnchor) — no range gate
- `HoveredPullable` (RopePullable) — no range gate
- `HoveredGrapplePoint` (Vector3) — exact surface hit point for grapple
- `SwingAnimIndex` (int) — default 4 (wrench/air)
- `MeleeResource` (ResourceNode) — resource within melee range
- `HoveredInteractable` (IInteractionPromptProvider) — generic interaction target
- `HoveredGameObject` (GameObject) — delegates to `MousePointer.Instance`

**Hover types supported:** Resource, pickup (legacy), key-pickup (WorldItem), rope anchor, rope pullable, melee target (resource or hittable surface), generic interactable.

**How hover result is structured:** Each is a nullable/zero-default public property set in `Update()`. The aimer reads `MousePointer.Instance` for the single shared raycast hit, then runs component lookups via `GetComponentInParent<T>()` per hover type. Range is gated with `_interactionRange` (3f for pickups/resources) or `_meleeRange` (2.5f for melee).

**What works well:** Single raycast resolution (via MousePointer), no redundant per-system casts. Clean interface-based `IInteractionPromptProvider` for generic interactables. Range-gating per concern.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **Tight coupling to SolarpunkCharacterController** via `[RequireComponent]`. Should depend on an interface (`IMovementController` or similar).
- All hover resolution happens in one monolithic `Update()`. Should be broken into smaller resolvers or a composable `IHoverResolver` pattern.
- References `MousePointer.Instance` directly (singleton antipattern). Should depend on an injected `IMousePointer`.
- HoveredPickup is deprecated (WorldItemPickup) but still polled each frame — dead code.
- No null-safety on `_pointer` — early-returns silently if null, which can mask bugs.
- The `WorldAimPoint` fallback plane projection for misses assumes ground at player Y (breaks on cliffs/uneven terrain).

---

### 3. ToolHitContext / Hit System

**Files read:**
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Common/PlayerHitInfo.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/PlayerInitializer.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/WrenchSwingController.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/WrenchThrowController.cs`

**How hits flow:**

```
Mouse Click → WrenchSwingController.DoSwing()
  ↓ reads _aimer.WorldAimPoint, _aimer.HoveredGameObject, _aimer.SwingAnimIndex
  ↓ calls _playerInit.EmitHit(point, target, damage)
  ↓ PlayerInitializer.EmitHit() → ResourceManager.Instance.RaiseHit(info)
  ↓ ResourceManager.OnResourceHit event → ALL subscribed ResourceNodes
  ↓ each ResourceNode.HandleResourceManagerHit() checks if info.Target is this node
  ↓ if match: ReceiveHit(damage)
```

**PlayerHitInfo (`Common/PlayerHitInfo.cs`):** An immutable `readonly struct` with `Point` (Vector3), `Target` (GameObject), `Power` (int). Generic — describes WHAT happened, not WHO should react.

**PlayerInitializer:** Thin startup script. Subscribes to `ResourceManager.OnResourceHit` on enable (empty handler `HandleResourceHit`). Provides `EmitHit()` as the player-side publisher. Also has a debug hit key.

**WrenchSwingController:** Left-click swing. Reads `PlayerInventory.Instance.ActiveItemType` to determine if wrench is equipped. Reads `_aimer.SwingAnimIndex` for tool identity (1-4). Damage comes from `WrenchConfig.lightSwingDamage`. Cooldown 0.1s.

**WrenchThrowController:** Right-click charge+release throw. Spawns `ThrownWrench` projectile via `Instantiate`. Reads `_aimer.WorldAimPoint` for target. Boomerangs back. Only one throw airborne at a time.

**What works well:**
- Observer pattern through ResourceManager is cleanly decoupled — player doesn't know about resources.
- PlayerHitInfo is a value type (no allocation per hit).
- Wrench controllers are single-responsibility.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **No unified hit context.** There is no `HitContext` struct that bundles the hit point, hit normal, hit collider, tool type, damage power, and source. Each controller manually reads sub-properties from the aimer.
- **PlayerInitializer is an empty shell** — the `HandleResourceHit` callback is empty. The subscription/debscription pattern is correct but the handler does nothing.
- **No damage type / no element system** — `Power` is an int with no semantics.
- **No tool-effectiveness check** — the wrench always deals full damage regardless of the resource's `RequiredTool`. The tool switch is purely cosmetic (anim index).
- **WrenchThrowController does NOT emit hits** — the thrown wrench has no hit detection on impact (it just hovers + returns). No ranged damage.
- **Hard singleton dependencies** on `PlayerInventory.Instance` and `ResourceManager.Instance` throughout.
- **No hit VFX feedback pipeline** — hit visual is purely per-node (ResourceShake), nothing centralized.

---

### 4. ResourceNode + ResourceManager

**Files read:**
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/ResourceNode.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/ResourceManager.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/ResourceNodeConfig.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/ResourceDropSpawner.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/ResourceShake.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/ResourceDeathFall.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/EchoShardRoller.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Resources/DropEntry.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/HittableSurface.cs`

**ResourceNode** (`Player/ResourceNode.cs`):
- **Fields:** `_config` (ResourceNodeConfig SO), `_hitChannel` (ResourceHitChannel SO), `_onHitEvent` (UnityEvent), `_onDepletedEvent` (UnityEvent), `CurrentHealth`, `_depleted` flag.
- **C# events:** `OnDamaged` (Action<int>), `OnDepleted` (Action).
- **Properties:** `Config`, `CurrentHealth`, `MaxHealth`, `Health01`, `RequiredTool`, `DisplayName`, `AttackAnimIndex` (1-4 based on RequiredTool enum).
- **`ReceiveHit(int damage)`** — subtracts from health, raises `OnDamaged`, raises `_hitChannel.Raise()`, calls `Deplete()` if health ≤ 0.
- **`HandleResourceManagerHit(PlayerHitInfo)`** — subscribed to `ResourceManager.OnResourceHit`, checks ancestry to see if this node was hit, calls `ReceiveHit`.
- **Deplete()** — marks depleted, fires events, destroys self if no `ResourceDeathFall` component present.

**ResourceNodeConfig** (`Resources/ResourceNodeConfig.cs`):
- Fields: `displayName`, `requiredTool`, `maxHealth`, `drops[]` (DropEntry array), `dropScatterRadius`, `echoShardChancePerHit`, `echoShardItem`.

**DropEntry** (`Resources/DropEntry.cs`):
- Serializable struct: `item` (ItemDefinition), `dropChance`, `minCount`, `maxCount`.

**ResourceManager** (`Resources/ResourceManager.cs`):
- Singleton (`Instance`). Runs at -100 execution order.
- **Event:** `Action<PlayerHitInfo> OnResourceHit`.
- **Method:** `RaiseHit(in PlayerHitInfo info)` — fires the event. Debug-log optional.
- No other events, no resource registry, no tool-effectiveness logic.

**ResourceDropSpawner** (`Resources/ResourceDropSpawner.cs`):
- Subscribes to `_node.OnDepleted`. Spawns each DropEntry's items via `WorldItemSpawner.Spawn()`.
- Per-drop: random check, random count, scatter within `dropScatterRadius`.

**ResourceShake** (`Resources/ResourceShake.cs`):
- Subscribes to `_node.OnDamaged`. Runs a coroutine that nudges position along a random XZ direction with sinusoidal decay. Amplitude scales with damage dealt.

**ResourceDeathFall** (`Resources/ResourceDeathFall.cs`):
- Subscribes to `_node.OnDepleted`. Disables colliders, disables Billboard, runs a coroutine that topples + fades the sprite, then destroys the GameObject.
- Its presence tells ResourceNode NOT to self-destroy (fallback if absent).

**EchoShardRoller** (`Resources/EchoShardRoller.cs`):
- Subscribes to `_node.OnDamaged`. On each hit, rolls random vs `echoShardChancePerHit`. On success, spawns the echo shard item via `WorldItemSpawner.Spawn`.

**HittableSurface** (`Player/HittableSurface.cs`):
- Marks non-resource melee surfaces with a `SurfaceMaterial` (Wood/Metal/Rock). Derives `AttackAnimIndex` (1-4). Used by PlayerMouseAimer to drive tool-swap for cosmetic animation only.

**Damage flow summary:**
```
Player swing → EmitHit(point, target, power)
  → ResourceManager.OnResourceHit
    → [for each ResourceNode] if target matches → ReceiveHit(damage)
      → OnDamaged event
        → ResourceShake (position shake)
        → EchoShardRoller (chance-based currency drop)
      → if health ≤ 0 → OnDepleted event
        → ResourceDropSpawner (spawn configured drops)
        → ResourceDeathFall (topple+fade animation, then destroy)
```

**What works well:**
- Clean event chain. Components subscribe to `OnDamaged`/`OnDepleted` — easy to add new behaviours.
- ResourceNodeConfig is data-driven (SO) — designers can create new resource types without code.
- Drop spawn is decoupled via ResourceDropSpawner.
- Death animation is decoupled via ResourceDeathFall.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **No damage gating by tool type.** The wrench hits any node regardless of RequiredTool. The tool-to-anim mapping works, but no gameplay consequence.
- **ResourceManager is anemic** — it only relays one event. Should own a resource registry, tool-effectiveness system, and loot-table resolution.
- **No area-of-effect damage** — each hit targets exactly one node.
- **Hard singleton dependency** — every ResourceNode grabs `ResourceManager.Instance` in OnEnable.
- **No pooling** — ResourceNode destroys itself; no object pooling for frequent spawn/destroy.
- **UnityEvent vs C# event overlap** — both `_onHitEvent` (UnityEvent) and `OnDamaged` (C# event) exist. Dual pattern is confusing.
- **`_depleted` flag prevents double-fire** — good, but should be more robust (the event could fire from two paths).
- **HittableSurface doesn't take damage** — it only drives animation index. If you swing at a non-resource prop, nothing happens gameplay-wise. No destructible world objects.

---

### 5. Inventory — PlayerInventory, Pickup, Drop

**Files read:**
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/PlayerInventory.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/PlayerPickupController.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/PlayerDropController.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/World/WorldItem.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/World/DroppedItemMagnet.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/World/WorldItemSpawner.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/InventoryData.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/InventorySlot.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/ItemDefinition.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/ItemType.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/WorldItemPickup.cs`

**PlayerInventory** (`Player/PlayerInventory.cs`):
- **Singleton** (`Instance`), -50 execution order. Lives on a MANAGER GameObject (not on the Player).
- Owns `InventorySlot[]` runtime array (copied from InventoryData SO on Awake).
- **Events:** `OnSlotChanged(int)`, `OnActiveSlotChanged(int)`.
- **Public API:** `SlotCount`, `ActiveSlotIndex`, `ActiveSlot`, `ActiveItem`, `ActiveItemType`, `IsFull`, `GetSlot(index)`, `HasItem(type)`, `HasRoomFor(item)`, `TryAddItem(item, count)`, `RemoveOne(index)`, `RemoveStack(index, out removed)`, `RemoveFromSlot(index, count, out removed)`.
- **Signals pattern:** `SignalPickup()`, `SignalDropOne()`, `SignalDropStack()` — thin wrappers over the core API for readability.
- **Hotkeys:** 1-4 keys switch active slot.
- Slot 0 = wrench (fixed). Slots 1+ = general stacks.

**InventoryData** (`Player/InventoryData.cs`): SO config with `resourceSlotCount`, `_defaultSlots`.

**InventorySlot** (`Player/InventorySlot.cs`): Value-type struct with `item` + `count`. `IsEmpty`, `IsFull`, `MaxStack`, `SpaceLeft`, `Of(item, count)`.

**ItemDefinition** (`Player/ItemDefinition.cs`): SO with `itemId`, `displayName`, `icon`, `itemType`, `attackAnimIndex`, `maxStack`, `worldPrefab`, `autoCollect`, `isCurrency`, `currencyTarget` (IntVariable). `AutoCollects` = autoCollect || isCurrency.

**ItemType:** Enum: `None=0`, `Pick=1`, `Axe=2`, `Hammer=3`, `Wrench=4`.

**WorldItem** (`World/WorldItem.cs`): MonoBehaviour on ground items. Holds ItemDefinition + count. Implements `IInteractionPromptProvider` (returns "E Pick Up" prompt for non-auto-collect items). `Configure(item, count)`, `Reduce(amount)`.

**PlayerPickupController:** Reads `_aimer.HoveredKeyPickup`. On E key, calls `inv.TryAddItem(item, count)`. Destroys/reduces the WorldItem.

**PlayerDropController:** G key drops 1 unit from active slot. `DropSlot(index)` drops whole stack (for UI drag). Spawns via `WorldItemSpawner.Spawn()` with pop impulse, then suppresses magnet for `_reCollectDelay`.

**DroppedItemMagnet** (`World/DroppedItemMagnet.cs`): Auto-collect items fly to player after `_settleDelay`. Uses `PlayerAnchor` SO to find the player (no FindObjectOfType). `_flying` mode makes rigidbody kinematic and uses `MoveTowards`. On collect: currencies route to `currencyTarget.Add()`, items route to `PlayerInventory`. Supports `Suppress(seconds)` for drop delay. Partial-collection fallback if inventory fills mid-flight.

**WorldItemSpawner** (`World/WorldItemSpawner.cs`): Static class with `Spawn(item, count, position, popImpulse)`. Instantiates `item.worldPrefab`, configures WorldItem, applies pop impulse.

**WorldItemPickup** (`Player/WorldItemPickup.cs`): DEPRECATED. Superseded by WorldItem. Kept for legacy compilation.

**Currency routing:**
1. DroppedItemMagnet detects `item.isCurrency` → calls `currencyTarget.Add(_item.Count)` → destroys self.
2. No inventory slot involved. The IntVariable SO is mutated directly.

**What works well:**
- Clean separation: the runtime array is copied from the SO on Awake — never mutates the asset.
- Events-driven HUD binding (no polling).
- Signals pattern clarifies intent vs implementation.
- Stacking logic in `TryAddItem` is correct (fills partial stacks first, then empty slots).
- Currency routing is efficient — bypasses inventory entirely.
- PlayerAnchor SO for player discovery (vs FindObjectOfType).

**What needs refactoring:**
- **Hard singleton** — everything accesses `PlayerInventory.Instance`. Should use dependency injection or a service locator interface.
- **No serialization** — inventory state is lost on scene reload / domain reload. No save system.
- **No equippable item abstraction** — the wrench is hardcoded as slot 0 with `ItemType.Wrench`. Adding new tools requires spreading knowledge of ItemType everywhere.
- **No item validation** — `TryAddItem` accepts any item; no check for unique items, no check for tool vs resource.
- **DroppedItemMagnet re-checks room every 0.4s** while waiting — polling pattern. Should use an event from inventory.
- **WorldItemSpawner is static** — can't be mocked or overridden (e.g. for networked drops).
- **`WorldItem.Reduce()`** doesn't destroy the object when count reaches 0 — the caller must check externally.
- **No IInventory interface** — inventory is tied to the singleton. Cannot swap or test.

### 6. RobotBattery

**File:** `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/RobotBattery.cs`

**API:**
- `Instance` (static singleton)
- `Charge` (int, reads from IntVariable)
- `IsEmpty`, `IsFull` (bool)
- `AddCharge(int amount)`, `Drain(int amount)`, `SetCharge(int value)`
- `SetAutoDrain(bool on)`
- Properties: `Min=0`, `Max=100` (const)

**How it works:** -40 execution order. Owns an `IntVariable` SO. Every `Update()` if `_autoDrain` is on, drains at `_drainPerSecond` (default 1f/s). The drain is accumulated in `_accum` float and discharged as whole integer points. HUD reads via `IntVariable.OnChanged` event.

**What works well:**
- Clean IntVariable pattern — UI reacts to changes via SO event.
- Singleton with duplicate protection.
- Simple API surface.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **No battery cost integration** — actions (swing, throw, lasso) don't drain battery.
- **Drain is a flat placeholder** (`_drainPerSecond=1f`). No system for real costs (time, actions, equipped items).
- **IntVariable is non-[Serialized]** — battery resets on domain reload. Fine for MVP but needs save hook.
- **No low-battery state events** — no `OnLowBattery`, `OnEmpty`, `OnFull` events beyond the generic IntVariable.OnChanged.

---

### 7. TerrainEffectZone + SolarpunkCharacterController

**Files read:**
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Terrain/TerrainEffectZone.cs`
- `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/SolarpunkCharacterController.cs`

**TerrainEffectZone:** Trigger volume. Applies one of four effects:
- **Wind:** Adds force each physics step (`rb.AddForce(windForce)`), reduces steering control.
- **Water:** Lowers `SpeedMultiplier`.
- **Mud:** Lowers `SpeedMultiplier` + blocks jump while grounded.
- **Ice:** Lowers `SteeringControl` + sets `LowGrip=true`.

Uses `OnTriggerStay` (fires every physics step). Sets values on the SolarpunkCharacterController's public properties.

**SolarpunkCharacterController:** Force-based 2.5D character controller.
- **Movement:** Acceleration toward a target velocity (XZ plane). Input is `Horizontal`/`Vertical` axis.
- **Jump:** Impulse, gated by `IsGrounded` + `CanJump`.
- **Terrain interaction:** Properties `SteeringControl`, `SpeedMultiplier`, `CanJump`, `LowGrip` are reset to defaults at the end of every `FixedUpdate()`. TerrainEffectZones re-set them in `OnTriggerStay` (which fires within the same physics step).
- **LowGrip logic:** Ice mode — no braking when idle, momentum carries. Timer-based grace window so single-step trigger gaps don't kill the slide.
- **Grounded check:** Raycast from collider base.

**What works well:**
- Smart use of force-based movement — physics composes naturally with AddForce zones, drag, friction.
- Per-step reset of terrain modifiers prevents stale state when leaving a zone.
- LowGrip grace timer is a thoughtful solution to trigger gap flicker.
- Clean separation: zone sets properties, controller reads them.

**What needs refactoring:**
- **No shared terrain state** — each zone independently sets controller properties. No composite effect system (e.g., wind + water = different behaviour).
- **OnTriggerStay** is less reliable than `OnTriggerEnter/Exit` + tracking your own state. If the Rigidbody sleeps or teleports, the stay event can miss a frame.
- **No effect priority** — if two zones overlap, last OnTriggerStay wins (race condition).
- **Controller properties are public mutable fields** — any script can stomp them. Should be `{ get; set; }` on an interface or use a struct.
- **No terrain state SO** — zone-to-controller coupling is tight. Could use a `TerrainState` SO that aggregates all zone effects.
- **MoveInput reads Input.GetAxisRaw** directly — no input abstraction layer.
- **Jump is always the same height** — no variable jump.

### 8. RopeLassoController

**File:** `Assets/Flynn/Scripts/Player/RopeLassoController.cs`
**Also read:** `RopeLassoConfig.cs`, `RopeAnchor.cs`, `RopePullable.cs`

**Structure:** MonoBehaviour with `[RequireComponent(typeof(PlayerMouseAimer))]`.

**Public API:**
- `IsCharging`, `ChargeNormalized`, `IsPulling`, `HandPoint`

**How it works:**
- Hold Q to charge (no gameplay effect — fires on release regardless).
- On release: reads `_aimer.HoveredAnchor` and `_aimer.HoveredPullable` + `HoveredGrapplePoint`.
- Range-gated against `_config.minRange` / `_config.maxRange`.
- If RopePullable → `BeginPull(selfPull: false)`: reels object to player.
- If RopeAnchor → `BeginPull(selfPull: true)`: reels player to anchor point.
- Winch is force-based (AddForce) with speed cap. Self-pull suppresses steering (can't fight the reel).
- LineRenderer draws the rope from HandPoint to the far end while pulling.
- **Mud check:** reads `_controller.CanJump` (which TerrainEffectZone sets false on mud).

**What works well:**
- Clean dual-mode (pull object / pull self).
- Force-based winch composes with physics.
- LineRenderer rope is simple and effective.
- Collision detection via aimer raycast (no separate trigger volume).

**What needs refactoring:**
- **Terrain interaction is fragile** — the mud check reads `CanJump` as a proxy, which is a side effect of the mud zone setting that property. Should have an explicit `IsInMud` property on the controller.
- **No cooldown on failed grapple** — if you miss/out-of-range, the charge still consumed and nothing happens (poor UX feedback).
- **No break force** — the pull runs until distance or timeout. No collision/wall break detection.
- **LineRenderer re-enabled every frame** — minor, but `LateUpdate` writes to `_ropeLine.enabled` every frame whether pulling or not.
- **Hard singleton dependency** on `PlayerInventory.Instance` for the wrench check.

**Full source (21 lines):**

public class Billboard : MonoBehaviour
{
    private Camera _mainCamera;
    private void Start() { _mainCamera = Camera.main; }
    private void LateUpdate()
    {
        if (_mainCamera == null) return;
